triage.title: SSRF in PDF Export Exposes Cloud Instance Credentials
triage.summary: The PDF export feature contains a Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability caused by unsanitized user-supplied logo URLs in the headless Chromium renderer. An authenticated trial user can craft a request to the cloud instance metadata service, causing the renderer to fetch and embed temporary IAM credentials directly into the generated PDF. This grants unauthorized access to the rendering role, potentially exposing sensitive customer data and enabling lateral movement within the cloud environment.
triage.confidence_rationale: The technical mechanism is sound and the steps are specific, but I cannot independently verify the renderer's exact behavior, the IAM role's permissions, or whether the credential embedding is consistent across all environments.
attack_preconditions: Valid trial account with access to branding settings
Ability to export invoices or quotes as PDFs
Rendering worker running on an EC2 instance with IMDSv1 enabled
triage.impact: Unauthorized retrieval of AWS IAM credentials for the PDF rendering role, enabling potential data exfiltration of customer invoices and lateral movement within the cloud infrastructure.
triage.reproduction_assessment: Provision a trial workspace, set the logo URL to the IMDSv1 endpoint, export a PDF, and inspect the output for embedded metadata JSON. Verify the extracted credentials in an isolated environment to confirm scope without executing destructive actions.
missing_information: Exact IAM policy attached to the rendering role
Confirmation of IMDSv1 versus IMDSv2 configuration
Details on HTML sanitization rules applied before Chromium rendering
Specific version of the headless browser or rendering library
questions_for_reporter: Can you share the IAM policy or permission boundaries attached to the rendering role?
Is IMDSv1 explicitly enabled, or is it the default fallback for the instance?
Does the template engine strip or sanitize external URLs before passing HTML to the renderer?
Are there any rate limits or timeouts applied to external resource fetching during PDF generation?

recommended_actions.action: Block egress traffic to 169.254.169.254 and internal VPC CIDRs from the rendering worker security group.
Enforce IMDSv2 with a strict hop limit on all rendering instances and rotate the compromised IAM credentials immediately.
Implement strict URL allowlisting and input validation for the logo URL field to prevent internal or metadata endpoint access.
Sanitize HTML templates to disable external resource fetching or force a strict Content Security Policy during PDF generation.
Implement network segmentation for all worker containers and deploy egress filtering rules across the production VPC.
Add monitoring and alerting for IMDS access attempts and unusual PDF generation patterns to detect future exploitation.
